subject: Skyline Health: sudden throughput degradation — policy mismatch suspected
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@skylinehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyline SRE <sre-team@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: API errors / throughput drop — urgent

Hi Lauren,

Heads up: Starting ~08:50 PDT our environment began seeing a sudden drop in successful requests to Redwood. We're observing a burst of 429s and elevated 5xx rate from your endpoint for our account (account id HS-98234). Latency also spiked to ~1.8s median on requests that succeed. This is causing a cascade for our ingest pipeline.

We haven't changed traffic patterns on our side — small steady ramp. Can you confirm whether any rate limit or quota changes were pushed from Redwood this morning? We also saw repeated "burst window exceeded" entries in the small snippet we received from our edge.

We're available for a quick triage call; we can escalate to our procurement/Security if needed, but for now this is an operational outage for our ingestion.

Attached: small error tail (skyline_error_log_2028-09-04.txt) with repeated 429/503 entries.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Jones
SRE Manager, Skyline Health
Phone: +1 415-555-0192
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API errors / throughput drop — urgent

Emma — thanks for the report and the log sample. We're on it.

Immediate plan:
- Marcus (SRE) is bootstrapping triage and will check quota/burst enforcement and recent policy pushes.
- Monica (CS) will coordinate with your team on impact and temporary workarounds.
- Rohan (Prod) will validate whether any routing or model-fallback changes could be implicated.

Can you confirm the top-level request rate (requests/sec) you saw before the degradation and the spike size? Also please forward any additional logs that include the full timestamp and request ids.

I'll set up a short bridge (15 min) to make decisions. If this is a policy misconfiguration on our side we'll prioritize a temporary lift while we fix the root cause.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Emma Jones <emma.jones@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API errors / throughput drop — urgent

On Mon, Sep 4, 2028 at 09:28 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Emma — thanks for the report and the log sample. We're on it.

Quick findings from an initial pass (logs + control plane audit):
- At 08:47 PDT we rolled a zone-wide rate-policy change that inadvertently tightened the burst-window calculation for a set of reserved accounts. Skyline's reserved capacity profile was matched to an older burst profile and the new rule changed the background token refill behavior.
- The enforcement triggered token exhaustion for sustained traffic spikes; control plane returned 429s and the serving runtime started shedding load which also caused increased latency for tail requests.
- No model change or routing switch observed — this is strictly enforcement-level (rate/burst) behavior.

I've attached a snapshot of the effective rate policy for Skyline (rate_policy_snapshot_2028-09-04.csv) and a parsed error tail (skyline_error_log_2028-09-04.txt).

Mitigation applied at 10:00 PDT:
- Temporarily reverted the zone policy for accounts with reserved capacity and re-applied the prior burst refill parameters.
- Opened an emergency rollout to raise Skyline's burst allowance by 3x (temporary for 2 hours) to allow the pipeline to drain.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether Skyline sees recovery in the next 10–15 minutes.
2) If recovery occurs, schedule a postmortem with product and control-plane teams to fix the policy rollout flow and add a canary check for reserved-capacity accounts.

-- Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: rate_policy_snapshot_2028-09-04.csv, skyline_error_log_2028-09-04.txt
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Skyline outage — executive summary & ask (temporary policy override)

Team — FYI and quick decision needed.

Summary: A control-plane policy rollout this morning tightened burst-refill parameters in one zone. The change unexpectedly affected a cohort of reserved accounts, including Skyline Health (HS-98234), which then experienced token exhaustion and an uptick in 429/5xx responses. Marcus has reverted the policy and applied a temporary 3x burst allowance; the customer is currently recovering.

Impact: customer ingestion pipeline degraded for ~13 minutes (08:47–09:00); potential downstream delays to Skyline's internal analytics for that window. Customer is asking for:
- Confirmation that the incident is resolved (we should validate SLA hit exposure)
- Root cause remediation timeline (control-plane rollout guardrails)
- Consideration of a goodwill credit for the incident window

Ask: Approve a temporary uplift and a goodwill credit (suggested: 1 day of usage credit) to prevent escalation to procurement/legal. Also recommend an expedited postmortem and a policy rollout hotfix.

Please reply with APPROVE/DECLINE for the credit and confirm owners for the postmortem.

— Lauren
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API errors / throughput drop — urgent

Emma — following up. Our monitoring shows request success rates back to baseline and median latency reduced to pre-incident levels. Action summary:

- Root cause: unintended zone policy rollout changed burst token refill for reserved accounts; enforcement produced 429s and transient latency.
- Immediate mitigations: policy revert at 10:00 PDT + temporary 3x burst allowance for 2 hours (expired at 12:00 PDT).
- Compensating actions: we will run an SLO impact calc and propose a credit if there is measurable SLA exposure.
- Prevention: adding a canary check for reserved-capacity accounts to the rollout pipeline and a postmortem scheduled tomorrow at 11:00 PDT. Marcus will lead the fix; Rohan will own rollout guardrails.

Can you confirm you see normal behavior on your side? If so I'll close the bridge and coordinate the postmortem invite.

Thanks again for patience — sorry for the disruption.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-latency-graphs-0904.png
